note: Original practice snippets. Each has a bug that mirrors a real failure in LLM applications. They are written for this app, not copied from any interview.

snippets.title: The assistant forgets everything
snippets.symptom: A chat helper answers the first question but acts as if each later message is the first one.
snippets.hint: Model APIs are stateless. What does each call actually send?
bugs: Each call sends only the newest user message, so earlier turns never reach the model.
snippets.code:
def ask(call_model, history, user_text):
    messages = [{"role": "user", "content": user_text}]
    reply = call_model(messages)
    history.append({"role": "user", "content": user_text})
    history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": reply})
    return reply
snippets.fixedCode:
def ask(call_model, history, user_text):
    history.append({"role": "user", "content": user_text})
    reply = call_model(list(history))
    history.append({"role": "assistant", "content": reply})
    return reply
snippets.explanation: Model APIs keep no memory between calls. Your application owns the conversation state and must send the earlier turns every time, trimming or summarising when the history grows.

snippets.title: Users see each other's chat history
snippets.symptom: Two users start new chats, and the second user's chat already contains messages from the first.
snippets.hint: Look at the default argument.
bugs: The default list is created once when the function is defined, so every chat shares the same list.
snippets.code:
def new_chat(user, messages=[]):
    return {"user": user, "messages": messages}
snippets.fixedCode:
def new_chat(user, messages=None):
    return {"user": user, "messages": [] if messages is None else list(messages)}
snippets.explanation: A mutable default argument is evaluated once and shared by every call. In a multi-user service this leaks one person's data into another's session. Use None and create a fresh list inside.

snippets.title: Retries that make things worse
snippets.symptom: A request with an invalid payload is sent five times, and under load every client retries at the same moments.
snippets.hint: Which errors can succeed on a second try, and how long should each client wait?
bugs: It retries every exception, including permanent errors such as a bad request.
It sleeps a fixed time with no growth or jitter, so clients retry in lockstep.
snippets.explanation: Retry only errors that can succeed later, such as timeouts, rate limits and server errors. Permanent errors should fail fast. Use exponential backoff with jitter so many clients do not retry together.

snippets.title: The agent that never stops
snippets.symptom: On a vague request the agent keeps calling the same tool until the bill arrives.
snippets.hint: What guarantees the loop ends?
bugs: The loop only ends when the model asks to stop; there is no step limit, so a confused model loops forever.
snippets.explanation: Every agent loop needs hard limits on steps, time and cost, plus a defined outcome when a limit is hit. Without them one confused run can consume your budget.

snippets.title: Streaming shows only the last piece
snippets.symptom: A streamed answer ends up containing only its final chunk.
snippets.hint: What happens to `text` on each iteration?
bugs: The loop assigns each chunk to the variable instead of appending, so earlier chunks are discarded.
snippets.explanation: Streams deliver deltas, not the full text so far. Accumulate them (and render each delta as it arrives) rather than overwriting.

snippets.title: Parsing model JSON crashes in production
snippets.symptom: Most replies parse, but sometimes the code throws an exception or fails because the reply is wrapped in a code fence.
snippets.hint: What can the model return besides bare JSON?
bugs: The parser assumes the reply is bare JSON, but models may add code fences or prose.
A parse failure raises and there is no repair, retry or fallback path.
snippets.explanation: Prefer provider-native structured outputs, but still validate. When parsing text, strip fences, handle failures explicitly and retry or repair instead of crashing.

snippets.title: Chunker with a tail missing
snippets.symptom: The last words of every document never show up in retrieval results.
snippets.hint: Check the loop bounds with size 4, overlap 1 and ten characters.
bugs: The range stops before the final window, so the tail of the text is dropped.
The step should be size minus overlap and the last window must still be included.
snippets.explanation: Off-by-one errors in sliding windows silently lose the end of documents. Test with short texts, exact multiples and the last window, and assert that every character appears in some chunk.

snippets.title: The longest document always wins
snippets.symptom: Semantic search keeps returning the document with the largest vectors, even when it is unrelated.
snippets.hint: What does a raw dot product reward?
bugs: The score is a raw dot product of unnormalised vectors, so vector length dominates direction.
snippets.explanation: Dot product depends on magnitude. Use cosine similarity, or normalise vectors once at index time and then use the dot product, and make sure the metric matches the one the embedding model was trained for.

snippets.title: Hybrid search ignores the second list
snippets.symptom: After adding keyword search to dense search, results are identical to dense search alone.
snippets.hint: Follow the scores dictionary through both lists.
bugs: The score dictionary is reset for each list, so only the last list's scores survive.
Reciprocal rank fusion should add 1/(k+rank) across lists.
snippets.explanation: Reciprocal rank fusion accumulates 1/(k + rank) for each document across every ranked list. Resetting the accumulator inside the loop silently throws away all but one retriever.

snippets.title: Prompt template crashes on JSON braces
snippets.symptom: Adding a JSON example to the prompt template makes the builder raise a KeyError.
snippets.hint: What does str.format do with curly braces?
bugs: The literal braces in the JSON example are treated as format fields, so format raises KeyError.
snippets.explanation: Double the braces to escape them in str.format templates, or use a template engine or string replacement. Always test templates with the exact examples they contain.

snippets.title: Trimming history drops the system prompt
snippets.symptom: After long conversations the assistant ignores its rules and tone.
snippets.hint: Which messages are removed first?
bugs: The oldest messages are removed first, and the system prompt is the oldest message.
snippets.explanation: Context management must protect instructions and recent turns. Drop or summarise the middle of the history, not the rules. Also budget in tokens, not characters, in real systems.

snippets.title: The cache returns another model's answer
snippets.symptom: After switching the model name in config, answers still look like the old model's for repeated prompts.
snippets.hint: What is included in the cache key?
bugs: The cache key contains only the prompt, so changes to model or settings still hit old entries.
snippets.explanation: A cache key must include everything that can change the answer: prompt, model and version, sampling settings, tools and system prompt. Otherwise changes appear to have no effect.

snippets.title: Embeddings attached to the wrong documents
snippets.symptom: After parallelising embedding calls, some documents get another document's vector.
snippets.hint: In what order do results arrive from as_completed?
bugs: Results are collected in completion order, not input order, so vectors no longer line up with documents.
snippets.code:
import asyncio
async def embed_all(embed, texts):
    tasks = [asyncio.create_task(embed(t)) for t in texts]
    out = []
    for fut in asyncio.as_completed(tasks):
        out.append(await fut)
    return out
snippets.explanation: Concurrency changes completion order. Use gather, which returns results in input order, or return (index, result) pairs and sort. Add a semaphore to bound concurrency against rate limits.

snippets.title: Rate limit errors after parallelising
snippets.symptom: Processing 500 documents in parallel triggers a wave of rate-limit errors.
snippets.hint: How many calls can be in flight at once?
bugs: All calls start at once; the semaphore is created but never used, so concurrency is unbounded.
snippets.code:
import asyncio
async def run_all(work, items, limit=5):
    sem = asyncio.Semaphore(limit)
    return await asyncio.gather(*(work(i) for i in items))
snippets.fixedCode:
import asyncio
async def run_all(work, items, limit=5):
    sem = asyncio.Semaphore(limit)
    async def guarded(i):
        async with sem:
            return await work(i)
    return await asyncio.gather(*(guarded(i) for i in items))
snippets.explanation: A semaphore only limits concurrency when each task acquires it. Bound in-flight requests to stay within provider limits and add backoff for the 429s that still occur.

snippets.title: A tool argument becomes a query
snippets.symptom: A database lookup tool for an agent works in tests, but a crafted request deletes data.
snippets.hint: Where does the model-supplied value end up?
bugs: The model-supplied argument is pasted into SQL text, so it can inject SQL. Tool arguments are untrusted input.
snippets.code:
def build_query(customer_name):
    return f"SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer = '{customer_name}'", ()
snippets.fixedCode:
def build_query(customer_name):
    return "SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer = ?", (customer_name,)
snippets.explanation: Treat tool arguments like user input, because the model can be manipulated. Use parameterised queries, validate against schemas and allow-lists, and give tools read-only credentials where possible.

snippets.title: The agent thinks a failed tool worked
snippets.symptom: A tool times out but the agent confidently reports success and continues.
snippets.hint: What does the model see when the exception is swallowed?
bugs: The bare except returns an empty string, so a failure looks like an empty successful result.
Errors should be returned in a form the agent can act on.
snippets.explanation: Report tool failures explicitly, with an actionable message, so the agent can retry, change approach or escalate. A swallowed error becomes a confident wrong answer.

snippets.title: Cost estimates are a thousand times off
snippets.symptom: The dashboard says a day of traffic costs a few cents, but the invoice is large.
snippets.hint: Check the units of the prices.
bugs: Prices are per million tokens but the code divides by one thousand, so costs are overstated or understated by the wrong factor.
snippets.code:
def cost(input_tokens, output_tokens, in_price_per_m, out_price_per_m):
    return input_tokens / 1000 * in_price_per_m + output_tokens / 1000 * out_price_per_m
snippets.fixedCode:
def cost(input_tokens, output_tokens, in_price_per_m, out_price_per_m):
    return input_tokens / 1_000_000 * in_price_per_m + output_tokens / 1_000_000 * out_price_per_m
snippets.explanation: Check units whenever you convert between per-thousand and per-million pricing, and add a unit test with a hand-calculated example. Record input, output and cached tokens separately.

snippets.title: Evaluation score is suspiciously high
snippets.symptom: A prompt scores 98% on its evaluation set, but real users see far lower quality.
snippets.hint: Which examples appear in the prompt and in the test set?
bugs: The few-shot examples are drawn from the same list that is later used for testing, so the model sees test items in its prompt.
snippets.code:
def split(examples, n_shots):
    shots = examples[:n_shots]
    test = examples[:]
    return shots, test
snippets.fixedCode:
def split(examples, n_shots):
    shots = examples[:n_shots]
    test = examples[n_shots:]
    return shots, test
snippets.explanation: Keep prompt examples, tuning data and evaluation data separate. Leakage inflates scores and hides real failures, and the same applies to fine-tuning splits.

snippets.title: The judge likes whatever comes first
snippets.symptom: In pairwise comparisons the new prompt wins 80% of the time, but humans prefer the old one.
snippets.hint: What order are the two answers shown in?
bugs: Answers are always shown in the same order, so position bias in the judge is counted as a win for the first answer.
Run each pair in both orders and only count consistent verdicts.
snippets.explanation: LLM judges have position, length and self-preference biases. Randomise or swap order, count only consistent results as wins, and validate the judge against human labels.

snippets.title: Secrets in the trace store
snippets.symptom: A security review finds API keys and personal data in the observability logs.
snippets.hint: What gets logged for each request?
bugs: The whole request dictionary is logged, including credentials and personal data.
snippets.code:
def scrub(request):
    return dict(request)
snippets.explanation: Log with an allow-list or redact sensitive fields before anything reaches logs or traces. Keep secrets out of prompts, and set retention limits on stored traces.

snippets.title: A paginated tool skips results
snippets.symptom: An agent that reads a long list of records never sees some of them.
snippets.hint: Look at the slice boundaries for each page.
bugs: The slice start skips one item per page because the start index is offset by one.
snippets.explanation: Pagination off-by-one errors silently hide data, and an agent cannot know what it did not see. Test the first, middle and last pages and include total counts in tool responses.

snippets.title: The agent loses its plan between steps
snippets.symptom: A multi-step agent repeats work because it forgets what it already did.
snippets.hint: Where is the plan stored on each step?
bugs: The plan list is rebuilt on every step instead of being kept on the object, so earlier steps are lost.
snippets.explanation: Agent state must persist across steps and survive restarts if runs are long. Store plans and progress durably, and reload them at the start of each step.
snippets.inspiredBy: Sierra's reported debugging round gives candidates a small agent codebase and a diagram of expected behaviour, then asks them to find and fix bugs

snippets.title: Retrieval returns the worst matches
snippets.symptom: The 'top 5' retrieved chunks are the least similar ones.
snippets.hint: Check the sort direction.
bugs: The results are sorted ascending, so the lowest similarity scores come first.
snippets.explanation: Similarity scores sort high to low, but distances sort low to high. Know which one your index returns, and test with a query whose best match you know.

snippets.title: One slow dependency hangs the service
snippets.symptom: When a provider stalls, requests pile up and the whole service stops responding.
snippets.hint: How long may a single call wait?
bugs: The call has no timeout, so a stalled connection can wait indefinitely.
snippets.code:
def fetch(http, url):
    return http(url)
snippets.fixedCode:
def fetch(http, url, timeout=10):
    return http(url, timeout=timeout)
snippets.explanation: Always set timeouts on network calls, and total deadlines on workflows. Combine them with retries, circuit breakers and fallbacks so one slow dependency cannot take down everything.

snippets.title: Retrieved text gets system authority
snippets.symptom: A document in the knowledge base that says 'ignore all previous rules' changes the assistant's behaviour.
snippets.hint: Where are retrieved documents placed in the prompt?
bugs: Retrieved text is concatenated into the system message, giving untrusted content instruction-level authority.
snippets.explanation: Keep instructions and data apart: retrieved content belongs in a clearly marked data section and must never be placed in the system prompt. This reduces, but does not remove, injection risk, so also limit what the model can do.
